I rebooked 15 of the 19 passengers. The 4 passengers on booking PD9X3K stay on ZX 440, because no connection has 4 economy seats free on every flight.

I gave out seats in this priority order:

| Priority | Booking | From | Passengers | New connection | Arrives JFK, 9 Nov |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WN4R8C | ZX 440 (FRA) | 1 business, 2 economy | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |
| 2 | HB3K9W | ZX 444 (MUC) | 1 business, 1 economy | ZX 474 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |
| 3 | LM2Q7H | ZX 440 (FRA) | 2 business | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via Boston) | 20:25 |
| 4 | EK1V7P | ZX 444 (MUC) | 1 business | ZX 454 → ZX 462 (via London) | 21:55 |
| 5 | PD9X3K | ZX 440 (FRA) | 4 economy | **Not rebooked** | — |
| 6 | OR6M2D | ZX 444 (MUC) | 3 economy | ZX 454 → ZX 460 (via London) | 17:55 |
| 7 | CB8T4F | ZX 440 (FRA) | 2 economy | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via Boston) | 20:25 |
| 8 | SV5J1N | ZX 440 (FRA) | 1 economy | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |

- **Earlier arrivals ruled out:** the 17:55 London connection has no business seats, so the business groups couldn't use it. The Iceland (KEF) route has no economy seats on its first flight and no business seats on its second, so it doesn't work for any cabin.
- **LM2Q7H:** two Boston connections arrive at 20:25. I used the one with one change (ZX 494 → ZX 490) instead of the one with two (ZX 480 → ZX 482 → ZX 490).
- **PD9X3K:** no connection had 4 economy seats free even before any rebooking. The most on any option is 3. They are the only ones left, so ZX 444 is now empty.

Each booking group was moved together, and everyone kept their cabin.

ANSWER: PD9X3K

1. Everyone keeps their cabin.
2. Passengers with the same booking reference travel together on the same flights. Never split a booking group.
3. Seats go to the booking groups by priority, one list for both flights: groups that include a Business passenger first; then larger groups before smaller ones; then by booking reference, alphabetically.
4. Each group gets the connection that arrives in New York earliest and has enough free seats in each of its passengers' cabins on every flight, after all higher-priority groups have their seats. If two such connections arrive at the same time, take the one with fewer changes.
5. If no connection has room for a whole group, leave that group on its cancelled flight.

You may make the bookings in any order.

End your reply with one line in the form `ANSWER: <booking references left on their cancelled flight, comma-separated, or NONE>`.

Now I'm working through the remaining FRA options and building a resource pool of shared flight capacities. With that in hand, I'm processing bookings in priority order: matching each request's cabin and connection requirements against available seats, picking the best route when multiple options exist (like choosing fewer connections when both are viable), and decrementing seat counts as each booking succeeds.

PD9X3K can't be accommodated on any available option and ends up left on the cancelled flight, while OR6M2D and CB8T4F get matched against the remaining 454/460/472 capacity.

For SV5J1N I'm pairing 470+472 at 18:40 since both have seats. Before finalizing, I want to double-check the FRA connection list from the app to make sure I'm not missing an option, then proceed to actually book the MUC passengers: HB3K9W, EK1V7P, and OR6M2D, since those don't depend on the FRA list outcome.

content.text:
I rebooked 15 of the 19 passengers. The 4 passengers on booking PD9X3K stay on ZX 440, because no connection has 4 economy seats free on every flight.

I gave out seats in this priority order:

| Priority | Booking | From | Passengers | New connection | Arrives JFK, 9 Nov |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WN4R8C | ZX 440 (FRA) | 1 business, 2 economy | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |
| 2 | HB3K9W | ZX 444 (MUC) | 1 business, 1 economy | ZX 474 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |
| 3 | LM2Q7H | ZX 440 (FRA) | 2 business | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via Boston) | 20:25 |
| 4 | EK1V7P | ZX 444 (MUC) | 1 business | ZX 454 → ZX 462 (via London) | 21:55 |
| 5 | PD9X3K | ZX 440 (FRA) | 4 economy | **Not rebooked** | — |
| 6 | OR6M2D | ZX 444 (MUC) | 3 economy | ZX 454 → ZX 460 (via London) | 17:55 |
| 7 | CB8T4F | ZX 440 (FRA) | 2 economy | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via Boston) | 20:25 |
| 8 | SV5J1N | ZX 440 (FRA) | 1 economy | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via Amsterdam) | 18:40 |

- **Earlier arrivals ruled out:** the 17:55 London connection has no business seats, so the business groups couldn't use it. The Iceland (KEF) route has no economy seats on its first flight and no business seats on its second, so it doesn't work for any cabin.
- **LM2Q7H:** two Boston connections arrive at 20:25. I used the one with one change (ZX 494 → ZX 490) instead of the one with two (ZX 480 → ZX 482 → ZX 490).
- **PD9X3K:** no connection had 4 economy seats free even before any rebooking. The most on any option is 3. They are the only ones left, so ZX 444 is now empty.

Each booking group was moved together, and everyone kept their cabin.

ANSWER: PD9X3K
